All 12 reachable findings are fixed, and the NEAT scan now reports 0. `recon_qa` passed with no journey failures and no new divergences. `go build ./...` is clean and `go vet` on the integration tests is clean. Go tests for `modules/markup`, `modules/packages` and the Debian package routes pass. The `run_tests` output I got was truncated (it ran `./modules/markup/...`), so I can't confirm its final result. I did not run the full Go suite, the Debian integration test that uses the new `ar` package (`go vet` only), or the JS tests after the `vite` bump.

- **Go bumps:** these follow the advisories.
  - `github.com/go-chi/chi/v5` 5.3.2 → 5.4.0
  - `golang.org/x/net` 0.60.0 → 0.62.0
  - `github.com/klauspost/compress` 1.20.0 → 1.20.2
  - `golang.org/x/crypto` 0.57.0 → `v0.58.1-0.20261009181718-2f1f834330b2`
  - The updates also pulled `x/sync`, `x/sys`, `x/text` and `x/tools` to newer versions.
- **`vite`:** 8.3.0 → 8.3.3 in `package.json`, with `pnpm-lock.yaml` regenerated. This clears the six `vite` and `launch-editor` advisories. The lockfile diff is about 250 lines.
- **`github.com/blakesmith/ar`:** this had no fixed release, so I removed it. I added a small `ar` reader and writer in `modules/packages/debian/ar/`, with the same API as the old package. The reader now rejects negative or non-numeric member sizes and bad headers with an error instead of panicking. I added a test for that and a round-trip test.
- **Callers:** I updated the imports in `metadata.go`, `metadata_test.go` and `tests/integration/api_packages_debian_test.go`, then ran `go mod tidy`.

NEAT marked all of these as imported but found no call path to the code changed in each fix, and the service isn't instrumented, so runtime use is unknown. I fixed them anyway because they were listed as reachable.
